rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: Landlords may collect a security deposit of no more than one and one-half times one month's rent, and annual increases may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Deposits must be held in trust in an interest-bearing account, interest belongs to the tenant, and the tenant must receive written notice of the bank and account details within 30 days.
rules.key_value: 1.5 times one month's rent; annual increase up to 10%
rules.penalty: If the tenant does not receive proper notice or interest, the tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% per annum interest to rent.

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied_two_or_three_family
exempt_if.text: The exception is an owner-occupied two-, or three-family dwelling.

exempt_if.name: seasonal_rental
exempt_if.text: This section of the Security Deposit Law does not apply to security deposits for seasonal use or rental (interest-bearing account provisions).

coverage.summary: Applies to most residential rental properties, including mobile homes.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings are exempt unless the tenant requests coverage in writing, and the interest-account provisions do not apply to seasonal rentals.

rules.quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.
